knowledge_point.title: Applying Green's Theorem to Regions With Holes

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186133886/concurrency-rlvnhq9g/plots/433df2b84dfc1e56d2ea.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{∂D}9y\,dx-4x\,dy,$ where $D$ is the region shown above.

The outer boundary is counterclockwise and each hole boundary is clockwise.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=9y$ and $Q(x,y)=-4x.$ So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=9,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=-4.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}9y\,dx-4x\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-4-9)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-13\,\text{d}A \\  & =-13{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =-13\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =-13\cdot (12\cdot 12-{2}^{2}-{4}^{2}) \\  & =-13\cdot (144-4-16) \\  & =-13\cdot 124 \\  & =-1612.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Green's theorem can be extended to include regions containing holes. In such cases, we can apply Green's theorem in the same way as before.

We have that $P(x,y)=9y$ and $Q(x,y)=8x.$ So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=9,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=8.
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}9y\,dx+8x\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(8-9)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-1\,\text{d}A \\  & =-1{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =-1\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =-1\cdot (16\cdot 12-{2}^{2}-{6}^{2}) \\  & =-1\cdot (192-4-36) \\  & =-1\cdot 152 \\  & =-152.\end{aligned}
